Download files using httr2

Source: R/utils-download.R
download_run_method.Rd

Download files sequentially with httr2, streaming each response to disk. Handles bearer-token authentication, retries, request throttling, progress reporting, and a summary of successful, failed, and skipped files.

Usage

download_run_method(
  urls = NULL,
  destfiles = NULL,
  token = NULL,
  show_progress = TRUE,
  max_tries = 20,
  rate_limit = 2,
  timeout = 3600,
  http_version = NULL
)

Arguments

urls

character vector. Non-empty vector of URLs to download.

destfiles

character vector. Destination file paths, in the same order and of the same length as urls.

token

character(1) or NULL. Bearer token added to every request when supplied. Default is NULL. Resolve token files or environment variables with get_token() before calling this function.

show_progress

logical(1). Show per-file progress messages and download progress bars. Default is TRUE; status and summary messages may still be printed when FALSE.

max_tries

integer(1). Maximum attempts per file request, including the initial attempt. Must be at least 1. Default is 20.

rate_limit

numeric(1). Request-throttling interval in seconds. Default is 2. Passed to httr2::req_throttle() as rate = 1 / rate_limit; the host-based token bucket controls the average rate and can allow bursts.

timeout

numeric(1). Timeout in seconds for each request attempt. Default is 3600 (one hour). This does not limit the total time across multiple files or retries. Connection establishment also has a 30-second timeout, subject to the overall per-attempt timeout.

http_version

integer(1) or NULL. Force HTTP version via curl's CURLOPT_HTTP_VERSION: 1L = HTTP/1.0, 2L = HTTP/1.1, 3L = HTTP/2. NULL (default) lets curl negotiate automatically. Pass 2L for servers that drop HTTP/2 connections (e.g., www.mrlc.gov for NLCD).

Value

An invisible list containing:

  • success: number of files downloaded and found to be non-empty.

  • failed: number of files whose download or non-empty-file check failed.

  • skipped: number of existing non-empty destination files.

  • failed_urls: character vector of URLs whose downloads failed.

  • failed_files: character vector of the corresponding destination basenames.

All five fields are always present. When no downloads fail, failed_urls and failed_files are character(0), including when every file is skipped.

Details

Existing non-empty destination files are skipped. Missing or empty files are downloaded, with missing parent directories created as needed.

HTTP 429, 502, 503, and 504 responses and transport failures are eligible for retries. When a server retry delay is unavailable, the configured backoff is a random delay between 0 and min(i^2, 30) seconds for retry index i. Server-provided retry delays may exceed 30 seconds. HTTP 500 is explicitly allowed by the error policy and is not included in the retry status set. Download validation checks that the saved file is non-empty; it does not validate its contents or format.

Individual request errors are recorded and remaining files are attempted. Files left by a failed request or empty download are removed. A warning reports failed filenames after the download loop finishes.

See also

get_token(), check_destfile(), download_preview()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
download_run_method(
  urls = "https://example.com/data.nc4",
  destfiles = file.path(tempdir(), "data.nc4"),
  max_tries = 3
)
} # }
